feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 0 (five 12 mm sensors at x ±0.02 m, y 0.05 m, mass 0.8, controller kp 3.0, base_speed 1.6) scored 52.28, the best so far, with progress 0.138 (oval) and 0.148 (s-bend) and line loss 1.0 to 2.0 per run. Iterations 1 to 5 each changed one lever (widening to ±0.03 m with 16 mm sensors, forward offset y 0.04 and 0.03, mass 0.7 and 0.6 kg, wheel radius 0.035 m, track 0.16 m). Line loss stayed at 1.0 per run in every case, and progress fell from iteration 1 onward. Steering oscillation stayed between 0.07 and 0.14, so the robot is not jittering. Decision rules for the next race: (1) If progress returns to about 0.14 on the oval and 0.15 on the s-bend with line_loss_events still at 1.0, the progress loss came from the sensing, and the line loss is a fixed point on the course. Stop changing sensing and ask for per-track telemetry on where the loss occurs. (2) If progress does not recover, the wheel radius and track changes are costing progress, so revert to wheel_radius 0.03 and wheel_track 0.12 (the iteration 0 values) with the same sensing. (3) If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2, the wider track is overshooting, so return wheel_track to 0.14 m.
requested_changes: Keep the iteration 0 sensing (five 12 mm sensors at x -0.02 to +0.02 m, y 0.05 m) with mass 0.8 kg. Basis: iteration 0 scored 52.28 with the best progress, and iterations 1 to 3 showed that widening to 16 mm sensors and moving them forward lowered progress without removing line loss.

If progress recovers but line_loss_events stays at 1.0, try sensor_size 0.008 with the same five positions at y 0.05 m. Basis: no iteration has tested a 8 mm footprint, and a smaller footprint gives a sharper line-position signal on the same layout. Test this only after the progress recovery is confirmed.

If progress does not recover with wheel_track 0.16 m and wheel_radius 0.035 m, revert both to the iteration 0 values (wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m). Basis: iteration 0 used these values for its best progress, and iterations 4 and 5 were the only runs with the larger radius and track.
